summary: Frank-Richard Hamm was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring (1940–1948) and held posts at Hamburg, the International Academy of Indian Culture, and Bonn (Professor, 1965).

Franklin Edgerton worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. After earning his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield (1906–1909), he served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Salisbury Professor at Yale University (1926–1953).

Franz Altheim worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1921–1928), where he held a post (~1928–1943) before positions at Halle-Wittenberg (~1943–1950) and the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1964).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctorate under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen (~1955–1959) and his habilitation at Frankfurt (~1960–1965), later serving as Professor at the University of Hamburg (1966–1971).

Franz Boas was a linguist and scholar who studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University, the Smithsonian, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (~1896–1942), which he founded.

Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy, Silvestre de Sacy, Karl Windischmann, and Johann Gottfried Eichhorn, attending Paris and Göttingen. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin (1821–1867).
Franz Ferdinand Schwarz specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Graz (~1953–1958) and later served there as a professor (~1976–1999).

Franz Heinrich Trithen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and as Professor of Modern Languages at the Taylor Institution (~1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Breslau, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey. He held chairs at Deccan College (1866–1881) and the University of Göttingen (from 1881).

Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bonn, Halle, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, where he habilitated and served as a lecturer (1829) and extraordinary professor of theology (1831).
Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who completed master's degrees at Freie Universität Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, followed by a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2003).
Franz von Erdmann was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Rostock (~1812–1815) and held a post at Kazan Imperial University (~1818–1845).

Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and as Professor at the University of Munich (2003–2019).
François Gros specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Lyon (~1951–1957) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002).

François Jacob earned doctorates at the University of Paris (~1944–1947) and Sorbonne University (~1950–1954). He held posts at the Centre National de Transfusion Sanguine, the Pasteur Institute (from 1960), and the Collège de France (from 1964).

Françoise Pommaret is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Sorbonne University, INALCO, and the University of Paris, later holding posts at INALCO, the Royal University of Bhutan (~2005), and the CNRS (Directeur de recherche, 2002).

Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who studied at INALCO under Heather Stoddard. She directed the Collège de France (2009–2015) and held leadership positions at INALCO, including head of the Tibetan department (2011) and department director (2013–2014).

Fred Pfeil worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. After studying at Amherst College (~1967–1971) and Stanford University (~1971–1973), he taught at Stanford, Stephens College (~1976–1981), Oregon State University (~1981–1985), and Trinity College, Hartford (~1985–2005).

Freda Bedi was a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at St Hugh's College, Oxford (~1929–1934) and under Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1953), and founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery.
